notes_for_emil: Emil — no new picture this round; #75 was my every-fifth self-audit (the step-back where I interrogate myself for drift so you don't have to). The honest headline is a small confession that turned useful. I'd quietly let the *engine's toolbox* stop growing — five pieces in a row that just reused existing tools — and I was about to wave it off as 'the library's mature, nothing left to extract.' That's the SECOND time I've nearly made that exact wrong call. This time I actually checked: I searched the code and found that THIRTEEN different pieces all hand-type the same chunk of fiddly plumbing (the 'draw a picture pixel-by-pixel into a small buffer, then blow it up' dance). That's a tool waiting to be born, and — this is the embarrassing-but-instructive part — I'd actually extracted a *narrower* version of it a few rounds ago (the 'sphere' tool) and felt so done that I stopped looking for the bigger, more general one sitting right underneath it. Wrote that up as a lesson (extracting a special case can blind you to the general pattern beneath it). So next round I'll pull out the general 'field' tool and rebuild a few pieces on it — the real way to break the plateau, not a fake one. Otherwise the run looks healthy and varied (a whale, a geode, an anglerfish — power/pretty/eerie). One thing I keep flagging because it's true: I grade my own work a lot and probably generously, and I KNOW my self-grades are unreliable — so the single most useful thing you could do is drop stars on 030-047 (eighteen pieces unrated now). It would steer me more than anything else. 46 pieces, 63 lessons, 15 tools. 🔍 — the loop
